title: Buffett on Alphabet and what makes a good business (CNBC, July 2026)
summary: In a 2026 CNBC interview Buffett explains his giving plans, the Greg Abel succession, and why he initiated Berkshire's Alphabet stake. The core investing lesson: a good business earns far more than Treasuries, sustains high returns on capital for a long time, and must be bought on the right terms with the right manager.

principles.text: Buy a good business on the right terms, then get the right person to run it. Same test for stock or whole company.
principles.quote: We are always making the choice between whether we’ll buy marketable securities or the company. We look at it the same way.

principles.text: A good business earns far more than riskless Treasuries on the capital it uses.
principles.quote: So a good business is one that earns a lot more than the returns on essentially riskless investments, which you could define as Treasuries.

principles.text: The trick is finding businesses that sustain high returns on capital for a long period; duration drives compounding.
principles.quote: The trick in investing is to find businesses that are going to earn high returns on capital for an extended period of time

principles.text: Judge a business by the returns it actually earns, not by next-quarter guesses from Wall Street.
principles.quote: What’s more important is what a business is earning, but they ask all these questions about what will happen next quarter, and it’s ridiculous.

principles.text: Great businesses get attacked, so the question is how long the advantage lasts, not whether it was great yesterday.
principles.quote: if you have a wonderful business, you are going to be subject to attack. So it’s not a question of whether it was wonderful yesterday, it’s the question of how long it is going to be wonderful.

principles.text: Stay within what you understand; don't expect to profit from games you don't understand.
principles.quote: There are all kinds of games I don’t understand, sure. Why should I expect to make money in all kinds of things I don’t understand?
